senses.definition: To put something up so that it stands, or to build a structure.
senses.example: The workers erected a fence around the garden.

senses.definition: Standing straight up rather than bending or lying down.
senses.example: The dog stood with its ears erect.

senses.definition: A lack of something needed, or a weakness that stops something working well.
senses.example: A blood test showed that she had an iron deficiency.

senses.definition: The son of your brother or sister, or of your husband's or wife's brother or sister.
senses.example: My sister's son is my nephew.

senses.definition: To make a shape, memory, or difference less clear.
senses.example: Tears blurred her view of the road.

senses.zh: 模糊的影像；模糊的记忆
senses.definition: Something you cannot see or remember clearly.
senses.example: Without my glasses, the sign was just a blur.

senses.definition: A substance added to soil to help plants grow.
senses.example: We added fertilizer before planting the tomatoes.

senses.definition: A small imaginary being with magic powers, often shown with wings.
senses.example: In the story, a fairy helped the lost child.

senses.definition: The height of a place or object above sea level or the ground.
senses.example: The village lies at an altitude of 2,000 metres.

senses.definition: Light that hurts your eyes, or a long, angry look.
senses.example: I closed the curtain to block the glare from the sun.

senses.zh: 怒目而视；发出刺眼的光
senses.definition: To look at someone with anger, or to shine so strongly that it is hard to look.
senses.example: She glared at the driver who had blocked her door.

evidence.note: Checked both noun and verb, including light and angry-look senses; wording and examples newly written.

senses.definition: The process of finding people to join a company, group, or the armed forces.
senses.example: The hospital has started a recruitment campaign for nurses.

senses.zh: 方便实用的；近在手边的；手巧的
senses.definition: Useful or easy to reach; also, good at making or repairing things with your hands.
senses.example: Keep a torch handy in case the power goes out.

senses.definition: To see or show how things are different, or to make one thing different from another.
senses.example: Young children may find it hard to differentiate between these sounds.

senses.definition: To work with others on something; also, to help an enemy that controls your country.
senses.example: The two schools collaborated on a science project.

senses.definition: Things following one another, or the process of taking over a position from someone else.
senses.example: Three buses arrived in quick succession.

author: vocab_author_c

senses.definition: A woman whose job is to serve food and drinks at tables.
senses.example: The waitress brought us two bowls of soup.

notes: Server is a common gender-neutral alternative; waitress remains current.

senses.definition: A small part left after most of something has gone or been used.
senses.example: We used a remnant of cloth to repair the bag.

senses.definition: Left after most of something has disappeared or been destroyed.
senses.example: The park protects a small area of remnant forest.

senses.definition: A building powder that becomes hard when mixed with water; also, a material that sticks things together.
senses.example: The builder mixed cement with sand and water.

senses.definition: To join things with a hard-setting material, or to make a relationship or position stronger.
senses.example: Working together helped cement their friendship.

senses.definition: To say a poem or other text aloud from memory, or list facts aloud.
senses.example: He recited a short poem at the school concert.

senses.definition: To fight by holding and pushing someone, or to struggle with a difficult problem.
senses.example: She wrestled with the decision for several days.

senses.definition: A fight using holds and pushes, or a struggle to deal with something difficult.
senses.example: After a brief wrestle, he pulled the heavy bag free.

senses.definition: Unwanted involvement in someone's affairs, or signals that stop a device receiving clearly.
senses.example: There was so much interference that we could barely hear the radio.

senses.definition: To judge an amount, difficulty, or someone's ability as less than it really is.
senses.example: We underestimated how long the repairs would take.

senses.definition: A judgment that gives a smaller amount or lower value than the true one.
senses.example: Our first budget was a serious underestimate.

senses.definition: To make something less good, let food go bad, or give someone so much that they expect too much.
senses.example: The rain did not spoil our picnic.

senses.zh: 战利品（常用复数）；挖出的废土
senses.definition: Goods taken from a defeated enemy, usually called spoils; also, earth dug out during building or mining.
senses.example: The army divided the spoils after the battle.

senses.definition: Meat from a pig's back or side, kept with salt or smoke and often cooked in thin slices.
senses.example: He cooked eggs and bacon for breakfast.

senses.zh: 成熟；成熟稳重；金融产品到期
senses.definition: The state of being fully grown or sensible; also, the time when a loan or investment must be paid back.
senses.example: She handled the disagreement with surprising maturity.

senses.zh: 从句；分句；合同或法律条款
senses.definition: A group of words with a subject and verb, or one separate rule in a legal agreement.
senses.example: The contract includes a clause about early payment.

senses.zh: 强健的；结实的；稳健可靠的
senses.definition: Strong and able to keep working well when conditions are difficult.
senses.example: We need a robust system that can handle sudden increases in traffic.

senses.definition: Someone you love, a name used when speaking to them, or a person especially liked by a group.
senses.example: Good morning, darling. Did you sleep well?

senses.definition: Much loved, or very attractive and sweet.
senses.example: She keeps a photo of her darling grandson on her desk.

author: vocab_author_c

senses.zh: 专营店；客厅（较旧用语，美式拼写）
senses.definition: A shop offering a particular service, or an old-fashioned name for a room where guests sit.
senses.example: We stopped at an ice cream parlor after dinner.

notes: British spelling: parlour. Living-room sense is old-fashioned, not the sole main sense.

senses.definition: A short official report or news update, given in writing or on a broadcast.
senses.example: The evening bulletin included a warning about heavy rain.

senses.definition: The study of how living things relate to each other and their surroundings, or those relationships themselves.
senses.example: The new road could damage the ecology of the valley.

senses.definition: An extra item used with something or worn with clothes; also, someone who helps with a crime.
senses.example: The shop sells phone cases and other accessories.

senses.definition: Extra rather than main, or helping another part work.
senses.example: The machine has an accessory power supply.

senses.definition: To feel angry because you think something is unfair to you.
senses.example: She resented being blamed for someone else's mistake.

senses.definition: A flat outdoor area by a building; a row of joined houses; or a flat strip cut into a hillside.
senses.example: We had breakfast on the terrace overlooking the sea.

senses.definition: To cut a hillside into flat steps for growing plants or building on.
senses.example: Farmers terraced the steep slope to grow rice.

senses.zh: 间接的；迂回的；不直说的
senses.definition: Not happening in a straight or immediate way, or not saying something openly.
senses.example: The factory closure had an indirect effect on local shops.

senses.zh: 琐碎的；小气计较的；轻微的
senses.definition: Not very important, or showing too much concern about small things in an unkind way.
senses.example: They wasted the meeting on petty arguments.

senses.zh: 脾气；情绪；怒气；金属硬度
senses.definition: A person's usual mood or anger; also, the hardness and strength given to metal by treatment.
senses.example: He took a deep breath to avoid losing his temper.

senses.definition: To make something less extreme, or treat metal with heat to give it the right hardness.
senses.example: She tempered her criticism with a few encouraging words.

senses.definition: A flower or group of flowers on a tree or bush, especially a fruit tree.
senses.example: Pink blossom covered the cherry trees.

senses.definition: To produce flowers, or develop in a healthy and successful way.
senses.example: Her confidence blossomed after she joined the club.

senses.definition: A vehicle designed to travel beyond the Earth's atmosphere.
senses.example: The spacecraft sent pictures of Mars back to Earth.

senses.zh: 马拉松赛跑；漫长艰苦的活动
senses.definition: A running race of about 42 kilometres, or an activity that continues for a very long time.
senses.example: She trained for six months before running her first marathon.

senses.definition: Continuing for a very long time and requiring much effort.
senses.example: The two sides reached an agreement after marathon talks.

senses.definition: Highly respected because people think it is important or of very good quality.
senses.example: He won a prestigious award for his research.

senses.definition: Covered in ice, very cold, or showing an unfriendly lack of warmth.
senses.example: Drive slowly because the roads are icy tonight.

senses.definition: The killing of many people, especially those unable to defend themselves; also, a very heavy defeat.
senses.example: The memorial honours the victims of the massacre.

senses.definition: To kill many people who cannot defend themselves, or defeat a team by a very large amount.
senses.example: The report described how villagers had been massacred.

senses.definition: To encourage someone to act or make something develop faster; also, to urge a horse forward with a metal heel point.
senses.example: The prize spurred her to work even harder.

senses.zh: 刺激因素；马刺；山嘴；支线
senses.definition: Something that encourages action; a metal heel point used on horses; or a narrow branch of a hill or railway.
senses.example: The competition provided a spur to innovation.
collocations: on the spur of the moment

senses.definition: A long, deep, narrow opening in the ground or sea floor, including one used by soldiers for protection.
senses.example: Workers dug a trench to lay the water pipe.

senses.definition: A change away from an expected route, rule, pattern, or value.
senses.example: Any deviation from the agreed plan must be explained.

senses.definition: To make a high musical sound through your lips or a small instrument, or make a similar sound while moving.
senses.example: He whistled a tune while washing the dishes.

senses.definition: A small object you blow to make a sharp sound, or the sound made by it or by your lips.
senses.example: The referee blew her whistle to stop the game.

senses.zh: 挚爱；忠诚；专心投入；虔诚
senses.definition: Strong love or loyalty, or the time and care given to a person, activity, or belief.
senses.example: Her devotion to her students was clear to everyone.

senses.zh: 柴油；柴油发动机或车辆
senses.definition: A fuel used in many trucks and buses, or an engine or vehicle that uses this fuel.
senses.example: This truck runs on diesel rather than petrol.

senses.definition: The scientific study of stars, planets, and other objects in space.
senses.example: Her interest in astronomy began with a small telescope.

author: vocab_author_c

senses.zh: 疯狂荒唐的；精神失常的（非临床用语）
senses.definition: Extremely foolish or unreasonable; also, an older or legal way to describe someone with severe mental illness.
senses.example: It would be insane to drive through that flooded road.

notes: Not a respectful clinical label for a person. Everyday figurative and legal uses should be distinguished.

senses.zh: 令人不快的；讨厌的；不友善的
senses.definition: Causing discomfort or dislike, or behaving in an unfriendly way.
senses.example: There was an unpleasant smell coming from the drain.

senses.definition: The bones that support a body, or the basic supporting structure of something.
senses.example: The museum displayed the skeleton of a large dinosaur.

senses.definition: Containing only the smallest number of people or parts needed to operate.
senses.example: A skeleton staff kept the office open during the holiday.

senses.definition: To join or repair material using a needle and thread.
senses.example: Could you teach me how to sew on a button?

senses.zh: 使遭受；施加（伤害或惩罚）
senses.definition: To cause someone to suffer pain, damage, or something else unpleasant.
senses.example: The storm inflicted serious damage on the coastal town.

senses.zh: 泥泞的；沾泥的；浑浊的；含糊的
senses.definition: Covered or mixed with wet earth, or not clear in colour, sound, or meaning.
senses.example: We left our muddy boots outside the door.

senses.definition: To cover something with wet earth or make a situation harder to understand.
senses.example: The new claims only muddied the debate.

senses.definition: An animal with a hard shell that lives in water or, especially in American English, on land.
senses.example: We watched a sea turtle swim beside the boat.

senses.definition: A boat that regularly carries people or vehicles across a stretch of water.
senses.example: We took a ferry to the island.

senses.definition: To carry people or things between places, often making several trips.
senses.example: A small bus ferried visitors from the station to the hotel.

senses.zh: 影响力；杠杆作用；借债投资
senses.definition: Power to influence a result; the lifting advantage of a bar; or borrowed money used to increase an investment.
senses.example: The large order gave the buyer more leverage in the price talks.

senses.definition: To use a resource or advantage to achieve more, or use borrowed money to increase an investment.
senses.example: The team leveraged its experience to solve the problem quickly.

evidence.note: Checked influence, mechanical, financial, and verb-use senses; no investment advice intended.

senses.definition: Likely to stick to things; unpleasantly warm and damp; or difficult to deal with.
senses.example: The children washed their sticky hands after eating the cake.

senses.definition: After the time or event just mentioned.
senses.example: She moved to Paris in May and found a job shortly thereafter.

senses.definition: People officially trained and appointed to lead religious services, especially in Christian churches.
senses.example: Members of the clergy joined the local volunteers.

senses.definition: A state of great confusion, disorder, or emotional trouble.
senses.example: The sudden closure threw the company into turmoil.

senses.zh: 迁徙；移居；迁移数据或系统
senses.definition: To move to another place to live or work, often with the seasons; also, to move data to a new system.
senses.example: Many birds migrate south before winter.

senses.definition: The state of having no faults, or the process of making something as good as possible.
senses.example: The bread was baked to perfection.

senses.zh: 热衷的；渴望的；敏锐的；强烈的
senses.definition: Very eager or interested; able to notice things well; or strongly felt.
senses.example: She's keen to learn how to repair her own bicycle.

senses.definition: To make a long, high crying sound because of deep sadness, especially after a death.
senses.example: In the novel, a woman keened beside the grave.

evidence.note: Checked mourning verb. Retained but clearly marked literary, never primary.

senses.definition: The child or young of a person, animal, or plant; the same form is used for one or several.
senses.example: The birds stayed close to protect their offspring.

senses.definition: Related to numbers, shapes, and the rules used to study them.
senses.example: The students used a mathematical model to predict the result.

senses.zh: 想象中的；虚构的；虚数的
senses.definition: Existing only in the mind, not in real life; in maths, relating to numbers involving the square root of minus one.
senses.example: As a child, he often talked to an imaginary friend.

author: vocab_author_c

senses.zh: 确定方向；使适应；使面向
senses.definition: To find or arrange a direction, help someone understand a new situation, or aim something at a particular need.
senses.example: The map helped us orient ourselves in the new city.

senses.zh: 东方；东亚（通常作the Orient，旧称）
senses.definition: An old name for the countries of eastern Asia, normally written as the Orient.
senses.example: The old travel book used the term 'the Orient'.

notes: Verb must be primary; geographic noun is dated and capitalized in actual use, retained as explicitly labeled historical usage.

senses.definition: A collection of records kept for future use, or the place or computer file where they are stored.
senses.example: The town archive holds maps from the nineteenth century.

senses.definition: To store documents or computer data so they can be used later.
senses.example: We archive completed projects at the end of each month.

senses.definition: To stick to a surface, or continue following a rule, plan, or belief.
senses.example: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.

senses.definition: In a way that changes something deeply or makes it very different.
senses.example: Working from home radically changed her daily routine.

senses.definition: A tall upright support for a building, or a person or idea that gives important support.
senses.example: Trust is a central pillar of their working relationship.

senses.definition: Clothes worn next to the skin under your outer clothes.
senses.example: Pack enough clean underwear for the whole trip.

senses.definition: The presence or spread of unwanted or harmful substances in something.
senses.example: The laboratory tested the water for contamination.

senses.zh: 不安的；不自在的；不稳定的
senses.definition: Worried or uncomfortable, or not peaceful and secure.
senses.example: She felt uneasy about walking home alone.

senses.definition: The event of someone or something no longer being seen or found.
senses.example: Police are investigating the child's disappearance.

senses.zh: 马车；火车车厢；运输；仪态
senses.definition: A horse-drawn vehicle or train car; the transport of goods; or the way someone holds their body.
senses.example: We found two empty seats in the last carriage.

senses.definition: A wild animal like a small dog with a long bushy tail; also, a clever person who may trick others.
senses.example: A fox crossed the road and disappeared into the woods.

senses.zh: 使困惑；难倒（英式非正式）
senses.definition: To confuse someone so they cannot understand or solve something.
senses.example: The last question completely foxed me.

senses.zh: 送信人；信使；即时通信程序
senses.definition: A person who carries a message, or software used to exchange messages quickly.
senses.example: A messenger delivered the documents before noon.

senses.zh: 人行道（英）；铺筑的路面（美）
senses.definition: In British English, a path beside a road for walking; in American English, a hard road surface.
senses.example: Please keep your bicycle off the pavement where people are walking.

senses.definition: Slightly wet, often in a pleasant or useful way.
senses.example: Keep the soil moist while the seeds are growing.

senses.zh: 保留；保持；记忆保持；滞留
senses.definition: The act or ability of keeping something, such as staff, information, or water.
senses.example: Regular review improves the retention of new vocabulary.

senses.definition: To arrange for something to happen later than originally planned.
senses.example: We postponed the picnic until the weather improved.

senses.definition: Disagreement, a claim made in an argument, or the position of still having a chance to win.
senses.example: The cost of the project remains a point of contention.

senses.definition: A powerful vehicle used mainly to pull farm equipment or other heavy loads.
senses.example: The farmer used a tractor to pull the trailer.

senses.definition: A person or group that receives money, property, or another benefit.
senses.example: Students were the main beneficiaries of the new library fund.

senses.zh: 无助的；无能为力的；无法自控的
senses.definition: Unable to protect yourself, change a situation, or control a strong reaction.
senses.example: I felt helpless when I saw the house filling with water.

senses.zh: 芭蕾舞；芭蕾舞剧；芭蕾舞团
senses.definition: A type of stage dance using carefully trained movements, a performance of it, or a group that performs it.
senses.example: She started learning ballet when she was six.

senses.zh: 速度；速率（物理中含方向）
senses.definition: The speed at which something moves; in physics, its speed together with its direction.
senses.example: The sensor measures the velocity of the moving object.

senses.zh: 使和解；使一致；使接受；核对账目
senses.definition: To restore a friendly relationship, make different ideas or records agree, or accept an unpleasant situation.
senses.example: They tried to reconcile their different plans for the future.

senses.zh: 隔间；车厢包间；分隔舱；格层
senses.definition: A separate section inside a larger space, container, or vehicle.
senses.example: Keep your passport in the zipped compartment of your bag.

senses.definition: Making a lot of sound, especially sound that is disturbing or unwanted.
senses.example: The cafe was too noisy for a quiet conversation.

senses.definition: A remark or action that treats someone with disrespect or makes them feel hurt.
senses.example: She took his rude joke as an insult.

senses.definition: To say or do something that treats someone with disrespect.
senses.example: There is no need to insult people who disagree with you.

senses.definition: Very strong anger, or great force and violence.
senses.example: She was shaking with fury after hearing the lie.

senses.definition: To begin a new project or journey, or get onto a ship or aircraft.
senses.example: They embarked on a plan to restore the old school.

senses.zh: 自发的；即兴的；自然发生的
senses.definition: Happening naturally without planning or an outside force causing it.
senses.example: The audience broke into spontaneous applause.

senses.definition: Thin in an attractive way, or small in amount and barely enough.
senses.example: The path crossed the stream on a slender wooden bridge.

senses.definition: A flower or the state of flowering; a fresh, healthy appearance; or rapid growth of tiny plants in water.
senses.example: The garden was full of bright summer blooms.

senses.definition: To produce flowers or become healthy, confident, and successful.
senses.example: These roses bloom from spring until autumn.

senses.definition: A piece of jewellery worn around the neck.
senses.example: She wore a silver necklace with a small blue stone.

senses.definition: The outer edge of an area or shape, or the total distance around it.
senses.example: A high fence runs around the perimeter of the site.
